title: Embed rerank investigation runbook Apr29 2026
content:
Quick summary:
- Intermittent failures and latency spikes observed on embeddings->rerank pipeline since 2026-04-28 deploy (canary).
- Two distinct symptoms: (A) "Dimension mismatch" errors returned from rerank endpoint for some requests; (B) p95/p99 latency spikes to >= 2s for otherwise small payloads.
- Repro is flaky locally but fairly common in canary traffic. Recording commands, traces, hypotheses below.

Timeline / important facts (raw):
- 2026-04-28 02:10 UTC: canary deploy of rerank scoring service (serve v2.14.0, PR #2103).
- 2026-04-28 02:40 UTC: initial alerts for error-rate increase on rerank (error-rate ~3% from 0.02%).
- 2026-04-28 03:00-09:00 UTC: on-call triage; added temporary rate-limiting to canary.
- 2026-04-28 05:12 UTC: observed first DimensionMismatchError in logs (see snippet below).
- 2026-04-29 11:20 UTC: reproduced locally with small traffic generator (only when batching enabled).

Commands and minimal repro attempts (what I ran):
1) curl to embeddings endpoint (hosted) -> then call rerank endpoint using returned vectors (manual):

curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings 
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $RWI_TOKEN' 
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' 
  -d '{"model":"rw-sim-lite-1536","input":["doc1","doc2"]}' | jq '.'

# then POST to local rerank:
curl -s -X POST http://localhost:8080/rerank 
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' 
  -d '{"query_vector": [0.12, ...], "candidates": [[0.2, ...],[0.1,...]]}'

Note: when I use full-length vectors (1536 dims) pipeline works. The failures cluster when embeddings are downprojected to 1024 dims (see below).

2) small python harness (used to iterate quickly):

import requests
import time

E = requests.post('https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings', json={"model":"rw-sim-lite-1536","input":["q"]}, headers={'Authorization': f'Bearer {token}'}, timeout=10).json()
vec = E['data'][0]['embedding']
# simulate rerank batch (vary batch_size)
resp = requests.post('http://localhost:8080/rerank', json={'query_vector': vec, 'candidates':[vec]*BATCH}, timeout=20)
print(resp.status_code, resp.text)

3) traffic generator used by Diego: ./tools/traffic-gen --model rw-sim-lite-1536 --rerank-endpoint http://canary-rerank:8080 --batching on --qps 50 --seed 42

Error snippets (copied from canary logs):

2026-04-28T05:12:03.234Z ERROR rerank.service handler.go:182 "DimensionMismatchError: expected dims=1536 got dims=1024 (candidate_index=7)"
stack: rerank/scoring.go:78 -> rerank/serve.go:215

2026-04-28T07:03:10.451Z WARN  rerank.batcher batcher.go:97 "batch latency spike: 2347ms (batch_size=16)"

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) model/quantization mismatch: Some embedding sources are being served with an older quantized checkpoint (1024-d) mis-tagged as rw-sim-lite-1536. Downstream expects 1536 and throws.
   - Evidence: error explicitly says 1024.
   - Counter: our embedding service only advertises 1536 models now. Where are 1024 vectors coming from? Possibly older cached vectors or a fallback model used for cold cache.

2) batching + concatenation bug: when batcher assembles payloads it can accidentally splice vectors (drop trailing dims) when multiple shapes are present in same batch. Could be a simple slice/copy bug in scorer that assumes fixed-length preallocated buffer.
   - Evidence: failures correlated with batch_size>8 and spikes in batch latency. Repro found locally only when batching enabled.

3) truncated network payloads: proxies or LB chunking producing truncated JSON arrays that parser interprets as shorter vectors. Less likely but hard to eliminate.

4) stale cache / mixed-model routing: smart routing may fallback to a smaller, cheaper model during capacity pressure; rerank isn't validating shape.

Observations / telemetry collected so far:
- p50/p95/p99 latency (canary): 45ms / 350ms / 2.1s. Spikes mostly during 02:40-06:00 UTC window.
- Error payloads: ~70% dimension mismatches show candidate_index != 0 (i.e., some candidate vectors in batch are short).
- Canary only; prod not impacted (yet). Canary traffic mix includes synthetic short-docs + long docs.
- No obvious OOMs on canary pods but GC pauses in one pod at times of spike (see SRE trace id SRE-4987).

Quick experiments attempted (results):
- Disabled batching entirely on canary -> error-rate drops to 0.1% but throughput falls. Means batching is tightly coupled to failure.
- Force model variant "rw-sim-1024" locally to check behavior -> rerank throws no dimension errors (expected).
- Added vector shape validation in scorer (reject batch if any length != expected) -> immediately surfaces bad requests; metric shows ~0.5% of requests would be rejected.
- Increased request path logging for 1 minute to capture raw payloads -> captured 4 failing payloads, all show one candidate vector with length 1024 while rest are 1536.

What this suggests:
- The issue is not the embedding API returning wrong model for all requests. Instead, some requests in a batch contain mixed-dimension vectors. That points to either: a) the batcher coalescing responses from different upstream model variants, or b) a bug in the batching buffer that copies partial arrays when it hits a boundary.

Immediate mitigations tried (and effects):
- Rolling-restart canary pods after increasing log level -> temporary lull, but returned.
- Turn off batching in canary (config flag) -> errors drop. Good short-term mitigation.
- Add strict validation (drop & log) -> stops crashes but increases error surface for clients (we would return 400 for those requests).

Next steps / action items:
1) Capture raw payloads for 10k failed batches (already running an adhoc logging job).
2) Add instrumentation in batcher to log source-model-tag for each candidate (if available) to detect mixed-models within batch. Diego to add this (task assigned).
3) Reproduce with minimal two-worker setup: worker-A serving rw-sim-lite-1536, worker-B deliberately set to rw-sim-1024; create batcher that polls both and see if mixed shapes can occur. (Hypothesis: race in batcher pulling responses).
4) SRE: check LB/proxy for chunking/truncation config and any 413/connection resets around spike times. Linked SRE trace SRE-4987.
5) Product: pause canary rollout until we have a root cause.
6) Engineering: hotfix to validate shapes before scoring (already PR draft: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serve/pull/2107).

Notes to self / weird findings that might be useful later:
- The failing candidate_index tends to be >0 --- could indicate that the first response in the batch is from same worker as request origin and others come from pooled workers. Maybe the local worker returns correct shape but remote pooled ones sometimes serve 1024.
- I saw a single log where the embedding vector length is 0 (empty array). Suspect network timeout / partial JSON. That would cause downstream code to reuse buffer memory incorrectly.
- GC pause correlation: one canary pod had a 150ms STW around spike; if batcher copies from shared buffer during STW we could see corrupted partially-written vector. Hmm.

Useful snippets to paste elsewhere:
- curl payload example (embedding): {
  "model": "rw-sim-lite-1536",
  "input": ["hello world"]
}
- typical failing rerank request (trimmed): {
  "query_vector": [0.1, 0.2, ... (1536 dims) ],
  "candidates": [ [0.1,... (1536)], [0.2,... (1024 OOPS)], ... ]
}

Open questions / unknowns:
- Why are 1024-d vectors present in canary? Are we running an older worker image in the pool? Image digests: canary was supposed to be uniform. Need to audit image tags/digests at time window.
- Is there any in-memory buffer reuse in Go code that could truncate a slice if cap/len misuse occurs?
- Could the embedding service be returning downprojected vectors for some inputs (e.g., internal fallback for very short docs)?

If I were to summarize one-liner for PM/TL: "Batcher occasionally contains mixed-dimension vectors (1536 vs 1024) leading to rerank failures; disabling batching stops failures. Root cause likely in batch assembly or mixed-worker routing; more telemetry needed."

My immediate priorities (today):
- Keep batching disabled on canary until we have shape-validation PR merged + more logs.
- Run controlled two-worker repro (Avery + Diego).
- Add shape validation and a metric to count mixed-batch incidents and alert at 0.1% (so we catch early).

Scratch TODO (low-level):
- [ ] instrument batcher: log per-item model_tag + vector_len (lightweight sampling)
- [ ] add unit test for buffer-copy semantics (slice reuse)
- [ ] audit container image digests for canary pool on 2026-04-28 02:00-08:00
- [ ] coordinate with SRE on LB chunking/timeouts

End notes: this doc is messy, sorry. Will convert into a cleaner incident writeup once we have root cause. For now keeping it personal scratchpad for iterating quickly.

-- avery
